vision: Meril envisions improving the quality of human life through world-class healthcare solutions. The company strives to "add more to life" by innovating medical technology that alleviates human suffering and improves patient outcomes on a global scale.
mission: Meril’s mission is to design, develop, and manufacture clinically relevant, state-of-the-art medical devices that address unmet clinical needs. By committing to research & development, cutting-edge manufacturing, strict quality standards, and scientific education of its stakeholders, Meril aims to champion the alleviation of human suffering and enhance the quality of life for patients worldwide.
history: Meril Life Sciences was founded in 2006 as part of the Bilakhia Group’s diversification into healthcare technology. Established by the Bilakhia family in Vapi, Gujarat (India), Meril began with a vision of developing innovative medical devices within India. Over the years, the company has expanded its portfolio across multiple medical domains and has grown into a global medtech player. Key milestones include the development of notable products (such as the Myval transcatheter heart valve and MeRes100 bioresorbable scaffold) and strategic partnerships and investments (e.g., significant funding in 2022 to fuel global growth). From its inception as a single facility in 2006, Meril has rapidly evolved into a multi-national organization by the mid-2020s.
leadership: Meril is privately owned and led by the Bilakhia Group (the founding Bilakhia family). The company’s leadership team consists of experienced professionals and industry experts guided by the founding family’s vision. Under the Bilakhia Group’s ownership, Meril’s leaders emphasize innovation, quality, and global expansion. (Notably, the founder Gufic ‘Karsanbhai’ Bilakhia and family established Meril, and the company’s CEO and executive team continue to drive its mission of advancing healthcare solutions.) The leadership is committed to maintaining Meril’s standards of excellence in R&D and manufacturing while steering the company into new international markets and therapies.
global_presence: Meril is headquartered in Vapi, Gujarat, India, and operates in over 100 countries around the world. The company has a workforce of more than 4,000 employees globally. It has established 100% subsidiaries or direct offices in several countries, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Brazil, Russia, South Africa, Turkey, Bangladesh, and others. Meril has also set up operations in markets like China and Japan to strengthen its local presence. Through a network of regional offices, distributors, and partners, Meril’s medical devices are available across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, the Middle East, and the Americas. This broad global footprint enables Meril to serve healthcare professionals and patients on nearly every continent, providing training and support in local regions as needed.
facilities: Meril’s manufacturing and R&D facilities are state-of-the-art and expansive. The primary campus, known as Meril Park in Vapi, spans about 180 acres (with over 250,000 square feet of built-up area) and houses dedicated manufacturing units for its four main verticals: cardiovascular devices, orthopedic implants, in-vitro diagnostics, and endo-surgical products. These ultra-modern facilities are designed to meet and exceed global quality standards. Meril’s production plants strictly adhere to cGMP (Current Good Manufacturing Practices) and are ISO 13485:2016 certified. The company’s manufacturing lines are highly integrated – from raw material processing to final product sterilization – allowing complete in-house control. For example, in the vascular intervention unit (~40,000 sq ft with 10,000 sq ft of cleanrooms), Meril performs laser cutting, electro-polishing, drug coating of stents, and sterile packaging under one roof. The orthopedic implant plant utilizes robotic machining for precision (Meril was one of the first in India to use robots to manufacture error-free knee implants). Across its facilities, Meril maintains cleanroom environments and advanced equipment for critical processes. The company’s commitment to quality is demonstrated by various international regulatory approvals for its plants and products, including CE marking for Europe, US FDA approvals for select products, and certifications from regulatory bodies in Canada (CMDCAS), Japan (PMDA), Brazil (ANVISA), Australia (TGA), Russia (MoH), and others. These world-class facilities enable Meril to produce over 100 distinct products while ensuring the highest levels of product safety, performance, and consistency.
R&D: Meril’s research and development is a core strength of the company. The Meril R&D Foundry (located at Meril Park) is an interdisciplinary center with more than 150 dedicated R&D professionals. This diverse team includes biomedical, mechanical, and materials engineers; polymer and chemical scientists; clinicians and life-science experts; as well as specialists in electronics, software, and industrial design (such as CAD designers and 3D animators). Meril’s R&D culture emphasizes identifying unmet clinical needs and rapidly iterating solutions to address them. The R&D group operates on a “3-tier” innovation philosophy: (1) improving and iterating current products to better fulfill existing clinical needs, (2) developing novel products in emerging therapeutic areas that represent next-generation treatments, and (3) researching truly disruptive, futuristic medical technologies that could revolutionize patient care. This approach has led Meril to create products like the bioresorbable vascular scaffold (MeRes100), advanced heart valve systems (Myval TAVR), and orthopedic innovations. The R&D facility is equipped with laboratories for prototyping, biomechanical testing, material analysis, and even preclinical trial support. Meril also actively collaborates with global scientific advisors, clinicians, and research institutions to guide its product development. The robust in-house R&D, combined with these collaborations, allows the company to introduce new products with a quick turnaround, ensuring that Meril remains at the forefront of medical innovation.
core_values: Meril’s core values revolve around curiosity, innovation, and a commitment to improving lives. A guiding motto internally is encapsulated by asking fundamental questions – “Why? What? Which? When? How?” – which the team refers to as "questions that add more to life." Every person at Meril is driven to find answers to these five questions in the context of human longevity, the workings of the human body, and the evolution of medical treatments and technologies. By fostering a culture of inquiry and open-ended problem-solving, Meril encourages its employees to seek solutions that not only advance medical science but also make a tangible difference in patients’ lives. This inquisitive ethos ensures that the company designs, manufactures, and distributes devices with a purpose: to alleviate suffering and contribute meaningfully to healthcare. In practice, Meril’s values translate to maintaining the highest standards of quality, embracing innovation and new ideas, collaborating with healthcare professionals ethically, and focusing on patient-centric outcomes in all their endeavors. The ultimate goal that stems from these values is captured in Meril’s tagline – “Adding more to life” – reflecting the company’s dedication to enriching human health and life expectancy through its work.
training_and_education: Meril goes beyond manufacturing devices by placing strong emphasis on training and education through its Meril Academy. Meril Academy is a world-class training center (spanning ~100,000 sq ft on the Vapi campus) dedicated to the education of healthcare professionals – including doctors, surgeons, paramedics, and hospital staff. The Academy hosts a variety of programs, workshops, and hands-on training sessions led by global Key Opinion Leader (KOL) faculty. Some key features of Meril Academy’s approach include simulator-based learning (allowing practitioners to practice procedures in a controlled environment), live case demonstrations and distance learning (telemedicine) to observe real procedures, and a well-equipped skills lab often dubbed a “hardware play room” for device trial and practice. The facility also contains a modern auditorium, breakout rooms, and a comprehensive medical library. By providing access to international expertise and cutting-edge training modalities, Meril Academy helps medical professionals stay up-to-date with the latest techniques and devices. This in turn aids in the faster adoption and proper use of Meril’s innovations, ultimately benefiting patients. Meril’s commitment to education underscores its role not just as a device maker but as a partner to the medical community, empowering practitioners with knowledge and skills for better healthcare delivery.
CSR: Meril’s corporate social responsibility (CSR) efforts are primarily focused on contributing to societal development, especially in the field of education. According to its publicly available CSR policy, Meril Life Sciences Pvt. Ltd. formed a CSR Committee and formally adopted a CSR policy in June 2014 (revised in July 2020) to guide its initiatives. Historically, Meril’s CSR initiatives have been concentrated on educational programs – for instance, supporting schools, scholarships, or educational infrastructure in underprivileged areas. Going forward, the company’s CSR policy outlines that it may engage in a broader set of activities as defined under Schedule VII of India’s Companies Act. These activities include: eradication of extreme hunger and malnutrition, healthcare and sanitation projects (e.g., access to clean drinking water and preventive healthcare in communities); promoting education (including special education for differently abled individuals and vocational training for women, children, and the elderly); promoting gender equality and women’s empowerment; setting up homes or hostels for women, orphans, and senior citizens; ensuring environmental sustainability through initiatives in ecology, biodiversity, and resource conservation; protecting national heritage, arts and culture; supporting armed forces veterans and war widows; and promoting sports (with an emphasis on rural sports and nationally recognized sports). Meril’s CSR policy also explicitly states that any surplus arising from CSR projects will not be added to the company’s profits but will be reinvested into further social projects. The company’s management has expressed commitment to these causes, ensuring that Meril continues to be a socially responsible organization that contributes positively to the community and environment while it pursues its business goals.
careers: Meril fosters a dynamic and inquiry-driven work culture. The company often states that “the road to medical and scientific evolution is paved with answers to tough questions” – reflecting its encouragement of curiosity and problem-solving among employees. With a growing team (over 1,400 members as cited on the careers page, and expanding alongside global growth), Meril seeks individuals who are passionate about making a difference in healthcare. The work environment is described as one where asking questions and pursuing innovative answers is highly valued. Employees are empowered to take initiative in finding solutions that could significantly impact human health. Meril’s careers philosophy invites prospective team members to “join the evolution of modern science.” The organization provides opportunities to work on impactful medical products across various domains (cardiology, orthopedics, endosurgery, diagnostics, etc.), often alongside leading experts and using advanced technologies. Professional development is supported through continuous learning (via Meril Academy and internal training programs) and cross-functional rotations (as seen in programs like the Future Leaders Training Program). The company prides itself on an open, collaborative atmosphere where every individual’s contribution can lead to extraordinary outcomes in patient care. In summary, a career at Meril is positioned as a chance to be part of a mission-driven team that is innovating to add more years and quality to patients’ lives, with the full support and trust of management to explore new ideas.
